tasks.short: Assess repayment risk and recommend a credit risk grade.

steps.what: Retrieve the request and current exposure from the {OTHER} credit case system.
Read statement notes and credit history for material risk factors.

loop.input: Statement notes and credit history, with source pages and reporting dates.
loop.output: Cited risk factors, conflicting facts and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require source references; reconcile figures to the approved financial spread; analyst checks material interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per document; unresolved items enter the manual review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed fields miss qualifications, contingent liabilities and unusual explanations in free text.

steps.what: Compare repayment capacity under base and stressed assumptions in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Clarify material gaps with the relationship manager.
Weigh evidence, select a risk grade and justify any policy exception.
Approve and record the assessment in the {OTHER} credit case system.

tasks.design: The {DATA_PLATFORM} joins exposure from the {OTHER} credit case system to the validated financial spread and ratio pack, then calculates versioned stress scenarios. A bounded reading loop proposes cited risk factors from the {DOCS}; the analyst clarifies gaps, makes the judgement and approves the recorded assessment through the {WORKFLOW}. The lending decision remains with the delegated credit authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data, qualitative evidence and scenario assumptions sit in separate places. Unusual accounting and business risks resist fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces and reusable calculation code can connect the evidence. Bounded text extraction can prepare a cited reading pack; faster development reduces the cost of fitting it to local records.
tasks.still_hard: Forward-looking repayment judgement, weak evidence and correlated risks remain difficult. Natural-person credit assessments require additional legal and model-governance work.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether reported repayment capacity is credible, challenge optimistic assumptions and explain why an exception is defensible.
tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time challenging assumptions and selecting exposures for deeper review. Lending approval limits remain unchanged; the analyst can refresh review priorities between formal credit reviews.

reach.task: Prioritise a sector watchlist using shared stress scenarios.
reach.learn: Portfolio concentration, scenario calibration and the difference between individual and correlated risk.

evidence.claim: Consented credit-data gathering can use an integration without a model; the cited example concerns Netherlands mortgage applications.
A product drafts credit memos from financial spreads and deal documents; this supports preparation, not autonomous risk approval.
AI used to evaluate natural persons' creditworthiness falls within the AI Act's high-risk category, subject to its scope and exceptions.
A score can constitute automated decision-making when the lender gives it a determining role.
Scenario arithmetic and evidence retrieval are suitable for deterministic implementation; material risk judgement still needs accountable review.

assumptions: The baseline is a mid-size lender's commercial credit team; the {OTHER} slot means its credit case system.
Validated financial spreads and ratios are supplied by the ratio task; this task does not recreate them.
Judgement and clarification retain substantial time despite the high automation prior.
Build ranges cover one portfolio pilot with shared data components, not a full lending-platform replacement.
The access range includes permissions, GDPR assessment and employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Whether the portfolio includes consumers, sole traders, corporate borrowers or mixed cases.
Which exposure feeds, credit-history sources and interfaces are available and licensed.
Who may approve risk grades and which exceptions require escalation.
Whether employee monitoring is introduced and consultation is required under national rules.
Whether approved scenario assumptions and usable historical outcomes already exist.
research_questions: Which risk factors are missed when the reading loop is tested against previously reviewed cases?
How often do scenario results change the analyst's judgement rather than merely restate it?
Which current EU and national requirements apply to the actual borrower population and deployment date?
new_work: Check cited risk factors and resolve unsupported interpretations.
Maintain scenario versions, data freshness checks and source permissions.
Review changes in extraction quality and missing-data rates.
Record judgement overrides and investigate recurring policy exceptions.

tasks.short: Complete the loan application and submit an approved pack to the loan committee.

steps.what: Collect the request, approved credit memo and supporting evidence.
Complete application fields in the {OTHER} credit case system.
Write the loan request summary for the committee.
Check completeness, reconcile terms and approve the committee submission.
Submit the approved pack to the loan committee through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} gathers approved evidence from the {DOCS} and the {OTHER} credit case system, populates application fields and builds the committee pack. A deterministic generator reuses approved memo sections for the request summary; completeness and consistency checks support the analyst's release approval before internal submission through the {EMAIL}. The same checks provide relationship managers with a pre-submission readiness view.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applications, evidence and committee templates use different fields and versions. Analysts rewrite summaries and reconcile terms by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: A shared case identifier, versioned templates and reusable field mappings support deterministic assembly. Approved memo content removes the need for another writing loop.
tasks.still_hard: Bespoke terms, late changes and committee-specific requirements create exceptions. Submission readiness does not establish that the proposed loan should be approved.
tasks.human_edge: Spot material inconsistencies, decide whether the evidence is sufficient and defend the request when the committee challenges it.

ambition.what: Pre-submission readiness checks for relationship managers.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time copying fields and chasing missing attachments, and more time resolving material conditions before committee review. Credit approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare a committee agenda that distinguishes routine requests from material policy exceptions.
reach.learn: Delegated lending authority, committee information needs and escalation criteria.

evidence.claim: Credit memo drafting from spreads, deal documents and institutional templates is available today.
Application population, required-field checks and routing can use deterministic mappings and configured approvals.
Reusing approved text avoids an additional generative step where the required summary follows a fixed structure.

assumptions: The loan committee is internal; submission does not issue an offer, sign a contract or release funds.
The credit memo task supplies approved analysis, so this task counts application assembly rather than a second analysis.
The approved memo contains reusable sections that satisfy the committee's summary requirements.
The review step approves the exact pack, version and recipient list used by the submission step.
Build ranges assume shared case data and cover access review and consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Whether the committee requires a separate summary or accepts referenced memo sections.
Which fields and attachments are mandatory for each loan type.
Whether the {OTHER} credit case system supports draft writes and version locking.
Who can approve submission and which changes invalidate that approval.
Whether committee membership, confidentiality restrictions and recipient lists are maintained reliably.
research_questions: Which missing fields most often cause committee packs to be returned?
Can approved memo sections populate every required summary field without new interpretation?
Can the release mechanism prevent a changed pack from using an earlier approval?
new_work: Resolve failed field mappings and missing-evidence alerts.
Maintain committee templates, required-field rules and recipient lists.
Review changed terms and reapprove packs when necessary.
Investigate failed submissions and reconcile receipts to case records.

tasks.short: Generate validated financial ratios from customer financial statements.

steps.what: Collect financial statements and available figures from the {OTHER} credit case system.
Map statement lines into a comparable financial spread in the {SPREADSHEET}.

loop.input: Unmapped statement lines, source pages, reporting periods, currencies and the approved accounting taxonomy.
loop.output: Proposed line mappings with source amounts and explicit unresolved items.
loop.check: Use deterministic mappings first; tie totals to statements; check units, signs and periods; review ambiguous classifications.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per statement; unmatched or unreconciled lines require manual mapping.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured imports and fixed mappings handle known formats; unfamiliar labels and layouts need bounded reading.

steps.what: Run ratio calculations and assemble comparable periods in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Check ratios, reconcile exceptions and approve the financial spread.
Save the approved ratio pack to the {OTHER} credit case system.

tasks.design: An intake job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} imports statement figures from the {OTHER} credit case system and the {DOCS}, using fixed mappings before a bounded extraction loop handles unfamiliar lines. Versioned formulas in the {SPREADSHEET} calculate ratios, while deterministic checks flag reconciliation failures, invalid denominators and incomparable periods. After exception review, the {WORKFLOW} publishes the approved spread and ratio pack for analysis and reporting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Arithmetic is already automated in many teams. Manual imports, inconsistent statement mappings and weak source links leave substantial preparation and checking work.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable import code and validation rules can surround existing formulas. Bounded extraction handles unfamiliar statement formats without asking a model to perform arithmetic.
tasks.still_hard: Accounting treatments, consolidation scope, restatements and exceptional items can make mathematically correct ratios misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether statements are genuinely comparable and whether an unusual item should change the interpretation or calculation basis.

ambition.what: Monthly liquidity deterioration review for borrowers supplying monthly financial statements.

tasks.altitude: The analyst reviews mapping and comparability exceptions instead of rebuilding ratio packs. Credit decision rights remain unchanged; fresher validated figures support earlier review requests.

reach.task: Reconcile financial statement classifications and explain restatements.
reach.learn: Consolidation boundaries, accounting policy differences and treatment of non-recurring items.

reach.task: Build a liquidity trend view from approved ratio packs.
reach.learn: Period comparability, data lineage and suppression of misleading comparisons.

evidence.claim: Evidence extraction and financial statement checking with human sign-off are available capabilities.
A documented accounting deployment reports shorter financial statement review work; it does not establish savings for credit ratio generation.
Financial ratios, denominator checks and statement tie-outs can be calculated deterministically.

assumptions: Today's team already uses calculation programs; savings come mainly from mapping, preparation, checking and publication.
The {SPREADSHEET} contains reusable approved formulas; where equivalent configured calculations exist in the {OTHER} credit case system, use those.
Models propose source mappings and never calculate financial ratios.
This task produces the financial spread and ratio pack reused by analysis and reporting.
Build ranges cover a limited set of statement formats, with access review and consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which statement formats and structured imports dominate the workload.
Whether current formulas are approved, versioned and consistent across analysts.
Which accounting adjustments require analyst approval.
Whether source statements contain personal data or information about guarantors.
Whether monthly borrower statements are available for the proposed liquidity review.
research_questions: What proportion of statement lines can fixed mappings handle without a model?
Which validation checks catch incorrect units, signs, periods and consolidation scopes?
How much analyst time is spent on arithmetic versus data preparation and comparability?
new_work: Review ambiguous statement mappings and reconciliation failures.
Maintain approved formulas, mappings and accounting adjustment rules.
Check extraction performance on new statement formats.
Reprocess restatements while retaining earlier approved versions.

tasks.short: Prepare a source-linked credit risk report for decision-makers.

steps.what: Retrieve the approved assessment, ratios and evidence for the reporting date.
Build financial tables and risk comparisons in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Draft the risk rationale, uncertainties and recommended conditions.

loop.input: Approved risk assessment, validated report tables, cited evidence and the report template.
loop.output: Draft narrative with source references, stated uncertainty and unchanged approved recommendations.
loop.check: Bind figures to validated fields; require references for factual claims; flag contradictions and new recommendations for analyst review.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per report; unresolved sections revert to a factual template for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables and standard sections are deterministic, but case-specific explanations require synthesis of free-text evidence.

steps.what: Challenge the conclusions and approve the memo and intended internal recipients.
Archive the approved memo in the {DOCS} and attach it to the credit case.

tasks.design: A generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} binds approved assessment fields and ratio tables into a versioned template in the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop explains the approved findings with source references; the analyst challenges the narrative and authorises publication through the {WORKFLOW}. The same approved content can produce a short risk briefing for relationship managers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Analysts assemble tables, copy evidence and rewrite narratives across disconnected records. Templates do not reliably preserve the link between a claim and its source.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured assessments, reusable templates and bounded drafting can produce a reviewable first draft. Deterministic figure binding and source references make checking more focused.
tasks.still_hard: A fluent explanation can hide weak evidence or overstate certainty. Reviewers must test whether the conclusions follow from the evidence and remain current.
tasks.human_edge: Explain what the figures fail to capture, distinguish evidence from inference and defend a recommendation under challenge.

ambition.what: Approved risk briefings for relationship managers.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends more time testing explanations and discussing material risks, with less report assembly. Report approval and lending decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Turn credit findings into a concise decision briefing.
reach.learn: Decision materiality, conditions of approval and communication of uncertainty.

reach.task: Use approved risk findings to prepare an early arrears handover.
reach.learn: Collection triggers, permitted information sharing and separation of risk concerns from payment facts.

evidence.claim: Credit memo drafting from spreads, deal documents and institutional templates is available today.
The digest describes a European bank deployment through a vendor account; it does not establish independently verified savings for this team.
Deterministic figure binding and versioned publication can reduce transcription work without delegating the credit decision.
The consumer credit directive provides rights concerning explanations and human intervention in automated creditworthiness assessments.

assumptions: The risk analysis task supplies the approved judgement; this task presents and explains it.
The ratio task supplies validated financial tables; reporting does not repeat financial spreading.
The generator cannot introduce a new risk grade, lending condition or recommendation without renewed analyst approval.
The approval covers the exact published version and its intended internal audience.
Build ranges assume shared evidence services and include permissions, GDPR review and consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which report templates and approval levels are mandatory.
Whether current assessments separate source facts, assumptions and recommendations.
Which recipients may access borrower-level evidence.
Whether consumer-facing explanations are within this team's remit.
Whether evidence versions and retention schedules are already controlled.
research_questions: Can reviewers trace every material narrative claim to current evidence?
Which report sections need synthesis rather than direct reuse of approved text?
Does the short briefing retain the uncertainties and conditions that matter to relationship managers?
new_work: Review narrative claims, source references and uncertainty statements.
Maintain templates, drafting instructions and approved terminology.
Invalidate drafts when underlying assessments or evidence change.
Track publication versions and correct misleading or unsupported passages.

role.altitude: The week shifts from collecting figures and assembling packs toward challenging repayment assumptions, resolving exceptions and explaining material risks. Analysts retain accountable judgement; lending authority remains with the existing delegated roles.
reach: Work with financial risk specialists on sector stress and review priorities.
Work with accountants on statement comparability and unusual accounting treatments.
Work with financial managers on committee readiness and decision briefings.
Work with business intelligence analysts on timely, validated liquidity trends.
skills_to_grow: Financial data lineage and deterministic validation.
Accounting comparability and treatment of exceptional items.
Scenario design and portfolio concentration analysis.
EU credit-data requirements and applicable national rules.
Clear communication of evidence, uncertainty and policy exceptions.
role.ambitious_version: A shared credit insight service supplies validated ratios, current stress scenarios, committee-ready evidence and approved risk briefings. Analysts use that capacity to identify deterioration earlier and defend difficult credit judgements.
